title: Graduated model-alias sunset: opt-in gateway, telemetry contract, and rollback gates
creator: Asha Raman
description: Goal: Provide a clear, low-friction pathway to retire v0 model alias behavior by introducing an opt-in gateway for new alias semantics, a telemetry contract that defines signal thresholds for automated rollback, and client guidance that minimizes disruption for high-volume customers. This PRD defines requirements, scope boundaries, acceptance criteria, migration steps, rollout timeline, and operational gates. Rationale: many customers rely on implicit model alias redirects; abrupt alias removal creates silent quality regressions. The opt-in gateway enables progressive adoption while giving us measurable signals to detect regressions and abort sunset if necessary.
scope_changes: In scope: opt-in gateway API and header, server-side compat shim for 12 weeks, telemetry event schema and dashboard, SDK advisory updates, billing continuity checks, automated rollback gates. Out of scope: changes to dedicated/private control plane packaging, on-prem full-offline adapter, or rewriting existing customer SDKs (we provide guidance and an adapter library instead).
requirements: 1) Introduce X-Model-Alias-Optin header and /v2/alias/optin route to register client opt-in per API key. 2) Maintain compat shim for default (non-opted-in) traffic for 12 weeks after public announcement. 3) Emit a mandatory telemetry contract for opt-in calls and inference comparisons (schema v1). 4) Provide SDK adapters (node/python-go) that surface opt-in and fallbacks. 5) Billing must be invariant; no accidental double-charging during shadow testing. 6) Define automated rollback gates and a manual emergency abort playbook.
acceptance_criteria: Opt-in gateway accepts header and returns 200 with tokenized opt-in record and TTL metadata.
Compat shim serves non-opted traffic with <=3% additional p99 latency overhead in staging.
Telemetry events for opt-in and A/B comparisons conform to schema v1 and appear in console dashboard within 5 minutes.
SDK adapters released with integration tests covering opt-in + fallback and published to npm/pypi/go proxy.
Billing audit shows no double charges for customers in shadow comparison mode during rollout window.
Rollback automation triggers when model-quality delta exceeds configured thresholds and notifies SRE + PM + customer success channels.
migration_steps: Step 1: Build opt-in gateway route + header support; add permissive default behavior in runtime. Deploy to staging.
Step 2: Implement telemetry schema v1 and console dashboard prototype; run synthetic regressions to validate signals.
Step 3: Release SDK adapters and a minimal client-side example. Publish migration guide in docs and send to early access customers.
Step 4: Open opt-in program to beta customers; collect telemetry for 4 weeks and run automated A/B comparisons (shadow baseline vs opt-in behavior).
Step 5: Gradual enforcement: start converting a small percentage of traffic to new alias semantics for opted-in keys only; monitor gates for 2 weeks.
Step 6: Announce deprecation window for default behavior (12 weeks); maintain compat shim for non-opted-in traffic during the window.
Step 7: If all telemetry passes, begin phased removal of compat shim by customer cohorts; if gates fail, execute rollback playbook and extend compatibility period.
rollout_timeline: Week 0-2: implementation + staging validation. Week 3-6: telemetry dashboard + SDK release + early access invite. Week 7-10: beta opt-in and shadow comparisons. Week 11: announce public deprecation window (12 weeks). Week 12-24: compat shim maintained; phased cohort removals starting week 16. Week 24+: final removal for remaining non-opted keys if gates held. Timeline is conditional on telemetry gates (see rollback_criteria).
rollback_criteria: Quality delta: Opt-in traffic shows >5% regression on primary QA metric (response coherence or downstream eval) sustained for 48 hours.
Error budget: Error rate on opted-in pathways increases p95 by >2x baseline for more than 1 hour.
Customer reports: Two or more enterprise customers file high-severity regression tickets linked to alias change within 7 days.
Unintended billing: Any incident where shadow testing causes non-transparent additional charges to a customer.
telemetry_signals: inference.comparison.delta (payload: api_key, model_before, model_after, metric, delta)
notes: Design/Legal flagged two items: CA data residency for telemetry export (ENG follow-up) and customer contract language for 'implicit alias behavior' in SLA. CS recommends an invite-only opt-in beta for top-20 customers before public announcement. SRE needs an on-call runbook for rollback that automates routing and clears any shadow billing buffers. Follow-up action: schedule cross-functional readiness review two weeks before public announcement.
